cards.text: Six days before the Passover, Jesus comes to Bethany. That's the hometown of Lazarus, the man Jesus raised from the dead. Friend, I spent years in a junk drawer and I thought MY comeback story was good.

cards.question: Jesus is in Bethany, the hometown of Lazarus. What do they host for Him there?
At the dinner for Jesus, Lazarus serves while Martha, his sister, reclines at the table.

cards.text: Then Mary, Lazarus's sister, brings out about a pint of expensive perfume made of pure nard. Not a little dab behind the ears, friend. A PINT.

cards.question: Mary anoints Jesus' ___ with the pure nard perfume.
Mary has just anointed Jesus' feet with the perfume. What does she wipe them with?

cards.text: "And the house was filled with the fragrance of the perfume." Like a fresh batch out of my oven, nobody has to ANNOUNCE it.
But one of Jesus' disciples speaks up: Judas Iscariot, the one who was going to betray Him. And he has a question about that perfume.

cards.question: Judas asks why Mary's perfume wasn't sold. How much does he say it could have been sold for?
Judas says the money from Mary's perfume should have been given to the poor.

cards.text: Sounds generous, right? Hold on, friend. John tells us why Judas really said it.

cards.question: Judas didn't ask about the perfume money because he cared about the poor. He asked because he was a ___.
Judas had nothing to do with the money bag.

cards.text: So the man upset about wasted money is the keeper of the money bag, taking from what's put in it. That's the coworker running the office cookie jar, giving a speech about how fast the cookies disappear, with crumbs all over his SHIRT.
Judas has made his complaint about Mary and her perfume. Now Jesus answers him.

cards.question: Judas just complained about Mary pouring out the perfume. How does Jesus answer him?

answers.text: He tells Judas to leave her alone
He tells Mary to sell what's left
He tells Judas to go help the poor

cards.question: Jesus says Mary has kept this perfume in preparation for the day of His ___.
Jesus tells them they will always have the poor with them, and they will always have Him with them too.

cards.text: Meanwhile, word gets out. A large crowd of Jews learns that Jesus is there, and they come.

cards.question: The large crowd comes to Bethany not only because of Jesus, but also to see ___.

cards.text: Friend, I came back from years in a junk drawer and NOBODY lined up to see me. Lazarus comes back from the dead and he draws a crowd.
But the chief priests aren't lining up to see Lazarus. They start making plans.

cards.question: What do the chief priests make plans to do to Lazarus?

answers.text: Put him out of the synagogue

cards.question: The chief priests plan against Lazarus because, on account of him, many of the Jews are deserting them and believing in Jesus.

cards.text: Lazarus is living proof, walking around Bethany, and because of him many are believing in Jesus. That man doesn't even have to give a SPEECH.

findings.problem: Most of stop 1's choice cards can only be answered by luck. Nothing on the earlier cards lets a baker reason out card 2 (a dinner vs. a wedding feast or harvest festival), card 3 (who serves and who reclines), card 5 (feet vs. hands or shoulders), card 6 (her hair vs. a veil or towel) or card 9 (three hundred vs. two hundred denarii). That is 5 of the 8 choice cards in the stop, which is more than a few discovery questions.

rule.text: A few discovery questions are fine. Some moments can't be reasoned out, like where Jonah's ship is headed. A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.

findings.problem: The card calls Martha Lazarus's sister. That fact comes from outside the passage (John 11:1-2), but the card only cites John 12:2 and gives no reference for it.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: The card calls Mary Lazarus's sister. That fact comes from outside the passage (John 11:1-2), but the card only cites John 12:3 and gives no reference for it.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: "The man upset about wasted money" states Judas's feeling as fact. The text only says he asked a question (John 12:4-5). It never says he was upset.

rule.text: He can guess at a feeling, marked as his own ("I think," "I bet"). Never as fact.

findings.problem: This is a recap card. "Judas has made his complaint about Mary and her perfume" repeats stop 1, and "Now Jesus answers him" doesn't move the passage forward. Card 2 repeats the same setup anyway.
The card calls Judas's words a "complaint." The text says Judas "asked" (John 12:4).

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: The question says "Judas just complained." The text says Judas "asked" (John 12:4).

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: This card only repeats what card 6 just answered: the crowd comes to see Lazarus (John 12:9). It moves nothing forward. Its joke is also the same junk-drawer comeback beat as stop 1, card 1.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage.

findings.problem: The chief priests appear here for the first time, and the card never says who they are.

rule.text: The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The text says the chief priests plan to kill Lazarus "as well" (John 12:10), meaning they already plan to kill Jesus. No card carries "as well," so the baker misses that the plot against Jesus is already underway.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: The first sentence restates verse 11, which card 10 just answered: because of Lazarus, many are believing in Jesus. That makes it a recap, not a move forward.
